questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a destination in Europe. There needed to be a university that offered courses I found interesting, and that would be useful for my degree. In addition, Milan is a large city with many international students, which makes it possible to meet many new people from Denmark and the rest of the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once you were familiar with the different programs and platforms used by the university, they were easy to access and use.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were given a university email address through which we received emails explaining how the different processes worked. Additionally, we had the opportunity to try the courses and modify them if they did not meet our expectations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find an apartment, but Milan is an expensive city, so it takes some time to look through different websites and find something that is not too expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It costs roughly the same as renting an apartment in Copenhagen. Make sure you have a good contract and a fair agreement regarding the deposit. It is an advantage to live close to campus, as you do not have to spend as much time on transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You attend some introductory classes to see how the teaching will be structured. After that, you need to register for the different courses on the university’s website. Finally, you can access the course itself and check whether your name is listed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Professors and student advisors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. We were registered in all the classes we wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to some different information sessions and check out a subject. Double-check that you don’t end up having two subjects at the same time (it’s possible to study a subject from home in Milan).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels matched the teaching we have received in Denmark. Even though we also had MA courses, it was possible to keep up. The professors are good at helping with questions and guiding you.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was less formal. Sometimes you could risk having too many students in a class, and as a result, you might end up sitting on the floor. Besides that, it worked in much the same way. The professors used PowerPoint to support the teaching

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Digital society, Human resource management, The language of the media, and Corporate communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Digital Society

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Often, when you have to pay bills in Italy, you also have to pay a fee, which can make the total amount significantly higher

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
We did not need to buy books, so it was less expensive than I had expected.
The public transport was less expensive than I had expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Italy classes

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the international week social media, there are a lot of activities for exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try different restaurants, tak the train to the Como lake, Duomo di Milano

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Some things, such as paying bills, are done in a different system, so you just had to get used to it

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: paying bills, the language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The less expensive restaurants, the more relaxed exam culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have savings that you can use during your stay for unexpected bills.
2. Be open to meeting new people, and don’t be afraid to take initiative.
2. Have a good and organized folder with all your documents related to the exchange (you often need to use the documents multiple times).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Be away from famility and friends in Denmark

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
